description: Result `range` values are `[start_row, start_col, end_row, end_col]`: rows are 1-based, columns are 0-based UTF-8 BYTE offsets (tree-sitter convention, not character indexes), and the end is exclusive.

row.description: A single 1-based row (matches the `file:line` numbers in get_symbol/find_references output and your editor). Provide this or `rows`.

rows.description: Several 1-based rows in the same file to resolve in ONE call — e.g. every line of a stack trace or diff hunk. Row-only; results come back per row under `results`.

col.description: 0-based UTF-8 byte offset within the row (tree-sitter convention), NOT a character index — they differ on lines containing non-ASCII text. Same unit as the `range` columns every tool returns.

max_body_lines.description: Keep this many source lines per returned `body`, eliding the middle with an additional `… N lines elided …` marker line that reports the true line count. The serialized body may therefore contain up to `max_body_lines + 1` lines. Omit to use `default_body_line_limit`; explicit values are clamped to `max_body_line_limit`.

limit.description: Cap on how many `rows` are resolved in one call (batch path only). Defaults to the server `default_result_limit`, clamped to `max_result_limit`. The effective page size may be smaller than `limit` because of the server's serialized-byte budget (`max_response_chars`), which shrinks a page that would otherwise exceed the client's tool-result cap. Always follow `next_offset` to resume rather than assuming you received `limit` results.

offset.description: Stable pagination offset over the requested `rows` list (batch path only) — skip this many rows before resolving. Use `next_offset` from the response to resume.
